closed_findings.evidence: Baseline account/group/binding lineage and canonical cluster anchor verified. One predicate now governs selection, locked recheck and INSERT/UPDATE fence. Mutable rename of original group no longer loses ownership; foreign same-name tenant groups and noncanonical clusters are excluded. Test source covers these positive/refusal controls.

findings.title: Full old seed can recreate the blanket under a new group ID after rename
findings.evidence: The supported normal rename leaves system/module-relation-writers natural key unused. Pre-1031 service manifest at fe607b38 declares that group and its cluster fga_writer grant. Old and current module_seed_writer.go:208-214 UpsertGroup generate a random ID and upsert on (account_id,name); apply.go:303-326 creates groups before applying bindings. Thus full old seed after retirement creates a new group and new ACTIVE system fga_writer binding. This predicate matches only the baseline group ID, so its fence accepts the new blanket and its retirement selector also misses it. Current test at account_writer_world_integration_test.go:752 calls only GrantRelation on the renamed original group; it cannot detect full seed recreation. This violates acceptance section4 rollback nonrestoration, even if ingress is kept closed.
findings.fix: Prevent the actual legacy installation seed lifecycle from recreating its retired blanket after a supported rename/deletion, while preserving unrelated tenant grants; cover complete old service seed group-upsert plus grant sequence, not only GrantRelation against original ID. Do not broaden ownership to all same-named groups.

positive_checks: Exact historical assignment predicate includes is_system, group subject, immutable group/account IDs, cluster type and canonical ID, fga_writer relation and NULL role.
Original binding ID is recorded as provenance rather than required for matching, so new binding IDs for the same original group are correctly fenced.
Delta does not change admission/read-reuse, account authority or general validators.
